chief_complaint: sudden severe pain in my chest, back, and legs
hpi_details: 22F with a known history of Sickle Cell Disease presents to the ED with extreme, deep, throbbing pain in her chest, lower back, and thighs. It started suddenly 6 hours ago. She has not had a fever or cough. She states this feels like her typical 'pain crises'.
ideas: knows it is a sickle cell crisis
concerns: worried she won't get enough pain medicine fast enough

investigation_events.title: Urgent sickle cell crisis results
investigation_events.availability_message: The urgent sickle cell crisis results are now available; individualized analgesia should not be delayed.

core_concepts: Sickled red blood cells occlude microvasculature, causing severe ischemic pain.
Triggers include stress, cold, dehydration, and infection.
common_misconceptions: Labeling patients as 'drug seekers' due to high opioid tolerance and specific requests for strong medications.
dangerous_errors: Missing Acute Chest Syndrome (new infiltrate on CXR with fever, chest pain, hypoxemia).
management_principles: Rapid, aggressive IV opioid analgesia, IV hydration, treat underlying triggers.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

source_refs.title: UpToDate & National Evidence-Based Clinical Practice Guidelines 2026

reference_soap.subjective: 22F with HbSS presenting with severe, typical vaso-occlusive crisis pain in chest/back/legs.
reference_soap.objective: In severe distress, writhing. HR 110, SpO2 98%. Clear lungs.
reference_soap.plan: Provide rapid, individualized analgesia using the patient’s established opioid plan when available, assess oxygenation, and give IV or oral fluids only to correct dehydration while avoiding fluid overload. Obtain CBC, reticulocyte count, and focused evaluation for triggers or complications such as infection, acute chest syndrome, or severe anemia.

learning_objectives: Manage sickle cell pain crises effectively and compassionately.

teaching.one_liner: A patient with known sickle cell disease presenting with classic severe ischemic bone and muscle pain.

must_ask.say: Do you have sickle cell disease, and does this pain feel like your usual crises?
Was there anything that may have triggered this, like being cold, dehydrated, or having an infection?
Are you having any chest pain, cough, or trouble breathing along with the pain?
How does this pain compare to your previous sickle cell crises, and what usually helps?
Have you been drinking enough fluids, and have you had any fever?

history.answer: My chest, lower back, and legs started hurting terribly all of a sudden. It feels like one of my sickle cell crises, and I really need help with the pain.
It came on abruptly about six hours ago while I was sitting at my desk studying for exams.
The pain is deep inside my chest, across my lower back, and down both of my thighs. It is deep in my bones rather than in one spot.
It is a terrible, deep, throbbing ache that feels like my bones are being crushed in a vise.
It does not travel to my jaw or down my left arm, but it spreads across my lower back and both legs.
It has been severe and continuous for the entire six hours without easing up at all.
It is definitely a ten out of ten. It is excruciating.
Resting does not help at all because it started while I was sitting down, and trying to move around just makes it worse.
Changing positions or leaning forward does not make any difference. Taking a deep breath does not make it sharp or hurt worse, and pressing on my chest does not change it.
It is not related to eating at all. I haven't had any acid reflux, sour taste, or trouble swallowing.
I feel sweaty and nauseated because the pain is so intense, but I haven't thrown up, felt faint, or felt short of breath.
No, I haven't had any fever, chills, cough, or phlegm.
No, I haven't had a cold, sore throat, runny nose, or body aches recently.
Neither leg is swollen, and both thighs hurt equally. I haven't been on any long flights or stuck in bed recently.
No, I haven't noticed any rashes, blisters, or skin redness anywhere.
I am very distressed because of how bad the pain is, but I did not have a panic attack or numbness in my hands.
I don't have high blood pressure, diabetes, or high cholesterol, and I don't smoke.
I have never had heart disease or procedures on my heart, but I get these sickle cell crises two or three times a year.
No, I haven't had any injuries, falls, heavy lifting, or hard workouts.
I stayed up late studying for college finals, barely slept, and didn't drink much water yesterday. The stress and dehydration probably triggered this.
When I have a crisis this severe, oral pills never work. In the emergency room, only intravenous hydromorphone gives me relief.
I know this is a sickle cell crisis, but I am worried the medical team will delay giving me pain medication. I really need intravenous pain medicine quickly.
I was diagnosed with sickle cell disease when I was a baby, and that is my only chronic medical condition.
I had my gallbladder removed when I was twelve because of gallstones, and I have been admitted several times before for sickle cell pain.
I take hydroxyurea every day and a folic acid supplement. I tried taking ibuprofen at home earlier, but it did nothing.
I do not have any allergies to medications, foods, or latex.
Both of my parents carry the sickle cell trait, and my younger brother has sickle cell disease. Nobody has early heart disease or blood clots.
I am a college student studying biology, and I live in an apartment near campus with two roommates.
I have never smoked cigarettes, used e-cigarettes, or tried recreational drugs.
I do not drink alcohol at all because I know getting dehydrated can bring on a pain crisis.
My last period started two weeks ago, and my cycles come every twenty-eight days like clockwork.
I take oral birth control pills every day without missing doses, and there is no chance that I am pregnant.

exam.finding: Young female in severe distress, writhing in pain on the stretcher and diaphoretic, with mild mucosal pallor and no jaundice.
Blood pressure 126/80 mmHg, heart rate 110 beats per minute, respiratory rate 20 breaths per minute, oxygen saturation 98% on room air, temperature 36.9°C.
Mild conjunctival pallor and faint scleral icterus noted bilaterally.
Jugular venous pressure is normal without jugular venous distension.
Symmetric chest expansion with no deformity, bruising, or reproducible chest wall or costochondral tenderness.
Resonant to percussion symmetrically across all lung fields.
Clear breath sounds bilaterally with equal air entry and no crackles, wheezes, or pleural friction rubs.
Tachycardic with regular rhythm, normal S1 and S2, a soft grade 2/6 systolic ejection flow murmur, and no pericardial friction rub.
Abdomen is soft and non-distended with no tenderness, guarding, rigidity, hepatomegaly, or splenomegaly.
No peripheral edema in bilateral lower extremities.
Calves are supple, symmetric, and non-tender bilaterally with no erythema or palpable cords.
Skin is warm and diaphoretic with no rashes, petechiae, vesicles, or localized erythema.
Normal spinal contour without focal midline vertebral spinous process tenderness, though moving causes generalized discomfort.
